context: Eleanor Chen, born 1943-05-12, has frailty in the directory, although some historical GP frailty entries are marked resolved. She needs step-free access, lives with her husband, uses a landline, and attends a library group on Thursday mornings. No medications or allergies are listed in the available GP record; absence of entries is not a completed reconciliation. This separate, entirely fictional outpatient episode describes six weeks of dry cough, fatigue and 2 kg unintentional weight loss. No haemoptysis, chest pain, resting breathlessness, fever or night sweats were reported. At the authored assessment she was comfortable, temperature 36.7 C, respiratory rate 16/min, oxygen saturation 97% on air, pulse 78/min; chest examination found no focal crackles. Historical low white-cell/neutrophil results remain in the source record and require comparison; this episode does not close unrelated earlier tasks or the renal correspondence task.

events.text: Original instruction: Please arrange FBC, U&E and CRP to investigate fatigue and weight loss, reassess previously low white-cell counts, and document renal function. The ordering GP will review the released results and communicate the interpretation by landline. Specimen collection must follow the order; clinician review depends on result release. This retrospective investigation has since been reviewed and communicated; it is not a new order.

The FBC, U&E and CRP request was entered in the authored episode and accepted for processing. FBC required an EDTA whole-blood tube; U&E and CRP required a serum tube. Both tubes used this investigation reference. This is a retrospective order record, not a new live laboratory request.

Venepuncture was booked for {collection_at} in the ground-floor treatment room. Eleanor confirmed the slot by landline; step-free access and transport with her husband were confirmed. Booking and the planned collection time are separate from actual collection.

Identity and the request were checked. EDTA whole blood and serum specimens were collected at this clinical event time, labelled at the chairside and placed in the dispatch bag. Specimen IDs are {reference}-EDTA and {reference}-SERUM. No collection difficulty was recorded.

Both labelled specimens were handed to the scheduled courier for Northbank training laboratory. The transport manifest listed this investigation reference and both specimen IDs; dispatch did not yet establish laboratory receipt.

Northbank training laboratory received and accessioned both specimens. Patient identifiers matched the request; sample volume and labelling were acceptable, with no documented haemolysis or clotting problem. Receipt was recorded separately from analysis.

FBC, U&E and CRP analysis completed after laboratory receipt. Instrument quality-control checks were accepted. Values remained provisional until validation; no clinician review was established by this event.

Analytical checks and result validation completed for both specimens. The numerical values below were approved for release. Validation did not itself document delivery to the GP record or clinician review.

Authorised synthetic results were released to the GP in this retrospective episode. FBC: haemoglobin 132 g/L (115-165); white cells 5.4 x10^9/L (4.0-11.0); neutrophils 3.1 x10^9/L (2.0-7.5); platelets 258 x10^9/L (150-400); MCV 88 fL (80-100). U&E: sodium 139 mmol/L (133-146); potassium 4.1 mmol/L (3.5-5.3); urea 5.6 mmol/L (2.5-7.8); creatinine 75 micromol/L (45-110); eGFR 65 mL/min/1.73m2 (laboratory flag threshold 60). CRP 6.2 mg/L (0-5). These authored values belong only to this newly labelled episode and do not replace existing native laboratory reports. The laboratory reference ranges are synthetic source values, not a treatment protocol.

The ordering GP reviewed this investigation's released FBC, U&E and CRP. White-cell and neutrophil counts in this specimen were within the supplied ranges, unlike the older low values in the record. CRP was slightly above this laboratory's supplied range. The GP documented no explanation for persistent cough and weight loss from these tests alone; the separate CT request remained in progress. No medicine was started or changed in this authored review. Other unresolved source-record tasks were not closed.

The practice nurse spoke to Eleanor on her landline after her Thursday library group, confirmed identity, and relayed the GP's blood-result interpretation. Eleanor understood that blood testing had finished while CT investigation was still pending. This records an authored completed conversation, not a queued message or an actual telephone call placed by the seed.

The ordering GP documented closure of this blood-test request: results were released, reviewed and communicated. No further blood specimen was requested in this episode. The independent CT pathway and unrelated pre-existing tasks remained separate.

Original instruction: Please arrange CT chest for persistent dry cough and unexplained weight loss after clinical assessment. Radiology to vet the request and choose the protocol before booking. The referring GP will review the authorised report and communicate the outcome. This is a separate investigation from the FBC, U&E and CRP. This retrospective CT investigation has since been reported, reviewed and communicated; only the separately documented symptom follow-up remains open.

The CT request was received in the radiology work queue and was awaiting vetting. The indication and contact details were present. No protocol approval or appointment booking had occurred at this point in the authored episode.

The radiologist vetted and approved the CT request after reviewing the clinical indication. Protocol: CT chest without intravenous contrast to assess lung parenchyma and look for a structural explanation of the symptoms. Approval preceded booking. This non-contrast study was not a CT pulmonary angiogram.

CT was booked for {scan_at} at the Northbank imaging department. Eleanor confirmed by landline. A step-free route, assistance with transfers and transport with her husband were confirmed. The appointment avoided Thursday morning; no online app response was required.

At attendance the radiographer confirmed identity, indication and radiologist-approved non-contrast protocol, explained the scan and recorded agreement to proceed. Pregnancy was not applicable for this older adult. Mobility and transfer support were checked. No intravenous contrast was planned, so contrast cannulation and contrast-specific preparation were not applicable. The absence of an allergy list was not represented as proof of no allergies.

CT chest acquisition completed after positioning and breath-hold coaching. Eleanor tolerated the procedure. Coverage extended from lung apices to the adrenal region. No intravenous contrast was administered and no immediate complication was documented.

The image series was checked for adequate coverage and became available in the authored imaging archive. This stage establishes image availability only; the radiologist's authorised report was not yet available. No DICOM objects or image files are created by this seed.

Authorised retrospective CT chest report. Technique: non-contrast volumetric CT chest. Findings: mild linear dependent atelectatic change at both bases. No focal consolidation, suspicious pulmonary mass, pleural effusion or enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes by size criteria. Central airways are patent. Impression: no focal thoracic lesion identified to explain the reported cough and weight loss. Limitation: a non-contrast examination does not assess pulmonary arterial emboli and has limited vascular/soft-tissue characterisation. Clinical reassessment of persistent symptoms remains appropriate in the authored plan. The report was authorised and available at this event time; it had not yet been reviewed by the referring GP.

The referring GP reviewed the authorised CT report for this investigation and compared it with the presenting history and the separately reviewed blood tests. No focal explanation for symptoms was identified in the authored report. The GP documented that the report did not resolve persistent symptoms by itself and recorded a plan for symptom and weight reassessment. No new diagnosis or prescription was added to the native problem or medication lists.

The referring GP spoke with Eleanor by landline, explained the CT report and its limitations, and confirmed her understanding. She agreed to symptom and weight reassessment. The authored conversation included advice to seek urgent help for new haemoptysis, chest pain or worsening breathlessness. This is retrospective synthetic communication evidence; the seeder sends no messages and places no calls.

The practice care coordinator accepted responsibility for arranging a GP symptom and weight review by {follow_up_deadline}, with landline contact and step-free access if attendance is required. This is downstream work after CT report review and patient communication. The CT investigation itself is complete; the follow-up appointment has not yet been booked or attended. The separate native task is the single outstanding instruction created by this seed.
